findings.issue: The compiler's nested ABI-encode loops for FacetCut[] are printed as 'while True' loops whose exit test holds the whole rest of the function (the call and stop), with element offsets re-derived from nested calldata offsets in every condition; there is no source loop, but each encode is 40-50 opaque lines.
findings.rule: When the only exit of a loop is a test at its top followed by code that never returns to the loop, print 'while not test:' and put that code after the loop; bind nested calldata offsets (cd[p + cd[t] + ...]) of the current element to a variable per iteration.

notes: Reviewed against EraChainTypeManager / ChainTypeManagerBase and Diamond (zkSync era l1-contracts). The pack lists no source loop in the reached code: every while of the text (37) is a compiler loop - ABI decode of the calldata DiamondCutData and ChainCreationParams with validation, ABI encode of the same structures for keccak256 and for the calls to the chain (executeUpgrade / genesis upgrade), copies of bytes4[] selector arrays, zero-initialisations. All 58 ABI functions were read by structure (owner/admin checks, protocol version bookkeeping, upgrade cut hash checks, chain creation forwarding to the bridgehub/chain, the events). Only 4 P2 lines; the main external calls are resolved. No execution run.
summary: Faithful; there is no source loop, but the many nested ABI encode/decode loops for DiamondCutData are printed as opaque 'while True' loops that contain the rest of their function in their exit branch.
